From: Sarah Greene <sarah.greene@sparkpay.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T09:23:00Z
Subject: SparkPay DPA redlines for onboarding

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. We're ready to move forward but legal asked us to start DPA review now so procurement can align on signature lanes. I attached our initial redlines (SparkPay_DPA_initial_redlines.docx).

Quick Qs:
- Can Redwood accept DocuSign with SparkPay signing first?
- We need a summary of what evidence (SOC 2, SIG, CAIQ) you'll share during onboarding.
- Data residency: we'll be US-only for now, but please confirm SCCs/DPA approach.

We'd like to close the DPA this month if possible. Who should I expect as the Redwood signer?

Thanks,
Sarah Greene
Senior Counsel — SparkPay
[sarah.greene@sparkpay.com]

[Attachment: SparkPay_DPA_initial_redlines.docx (docx)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Greene <sarah.greene@sparkpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: SparkPay DPA redlines for onboarding

Hi Sarah — thanks for sending this over and for the timeline. Looping in Neha (Privacy) and Marissa (Legal ops) to triage the redlines and confirm signature mechanics.

Proposed next steps from Redwood: 
1) Privacy/legal will triage your redlines and produce a consolidated Redwood redline for clarity (target by EOD 10/18).
2) We'll confirm what evidence we can share during onboarding (SOC 2 attestation, redacted report; completed SIG Lite; CAIQ summary) — Neha will detail this.
3) For signature, DocuSign is fine. Typical route for new commercial deals is customer signs first -> Redwood legal/ops -> Redwood exec (if exec-stamp required). We can pre-authorize Marissa to e-sign for standard DPAs; if there are exceptional exec-level carve-outs we'll flag and escalate.

Can you confirm: primary procurement contact (email) and whether SparkPay requires signature from a specific position (CEO/CFO) or an authorized signatory? Also confirm whether PHI will be involved — that will change our HIPAA approach.

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

[Attachment: SparkPay_onboarding_checklist.pdf (pdf)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Greene <sarah.greene@sparkpay.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-17T08:15:00Z
Subject: RE: SparkPay DPA redlines for onboarding

Thanks, Jonas and Sarah — I reviewed SparkPay's initial redlines and did a quick matrix. High-level: most standard commercial requests are fine, but there are three areas that need negotiation/escalation:

1) Subprocessor carve-outs: SparkPay asks for prior written consent for all new subprocessors. We can propose a 30-day notification + right to object for critical categories instead of prior consent for every supplier.
2) Indemnity & consequential damages: we will not accept open-ended indemnity/liability increases — need specific language, Marissa will propose fallback language.
3) Retention & deletion cycles: SparkPay requested 1 year; Redwood's default is 3 years for backups and 30 days for customer data after termination — we can present a short-term retention carveout for onboarding data.

Evidence: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), completed SIG Lite spreadsheet, and CAIQ summary. I'll attach a comment matrix that maps SparkPay redlines to our stance. Please note HIPAA: if PHI may be processed we need a Business Associate Addendum (BAA) — please confirm.

Attachment: DPA_comment_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

I'll draft the consolidated Redwood redline and circulate by midday 10/18 so we can get alignment before routing to signature.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Privacy | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
